# Starter: FUTURE course dedup

This is a small, standalone TypeScript project (not part of the Berkeleytime
monorepo) modeling a real bug from Berkeleytime's course-data sync pipeline.

## Setup

```bash
cd starter
npm install
npm test          # run the test suite once
npm run test:watch  # rerun on file changes
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
```

## The task

`src/dedupe.ts` exports `dedupeCourses`, which is supposed to take the raw
list of course versions a periodic sync job pulls from the upstream system
(see `src/fixtures.ts` and `src/types.ts` for the shape and the specific
cases baked into the fixture) and return exactly one canonical row per
course, deterministically.

`dedupeCourses` is currently a stub -- it throws `not implemented`. Run
`npm test` to see every case fail. Your job is to implement it, based on
your own Round 1 design (or a revised version of it, now that you can see
the concrete types and fixtures), so that every test in
`test/dedupe.test.ts` passes.

Read the comments at the top of `src/dedupe.ts` and `src/fixtures.ts` first --
they describe the contract your implementation needs to satisfy and the
edge cases the tests check for. Do not edit the test file or the fixtures;
if you think a test is wrong, say so in your writeup instead of changing it.

This should take a competent engineer roughly 1-2 hours of the 3-4 hour
slot, including using whatever AI tools you'd normally use. The remaining
time is for the code review discussion.

## AI tool usage

Use AI tools however you normally would for this kind of task. Please keep a
plain-text or markdown log of the prompts you used (a running log is fine --
doesn't need to be polished) and bring it to the code review. We're
interested in how you used the tool, what you kept vs. rejected, and where
you double-checked its output, not whether you used one at all.
